subject: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@healthscope.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up / next steps

Hi Lydia — thanks again for the convo today, really useful to hear about the triage flow and the safety bar you’re expecting for sensitive clinical prompts. Quick recap + proposed next steps: 

1) Recap from call
- Target product area: nurse triage assistant (symptom intake + next-step guidance).
- Primary requirements: high refusal accuracy on self-harm and controlled-medication requests, conservative suggestions for diagnosis, and auditable refusal signals for regulatory review.
- Throughput/latency: target 100 qps burst, p95 < 350ms for short prompts.

2) Model fit & eval plan (what we recommend first)
- Recommended candidate family: Llama-3 13B quantized variants (q4f16 and q8_0) and a tuned safety variant we maintain for conservative refusal behavior.
- Why: balance of latency/cost and better calibrated refusal behaviors in our benchmarks vs larger models for this workload.
- Plan: run targeted policy/refusal evals (prompt set attached) + 2k-sample clinical prompts (we'll redact PHI) to measure false-accept/false-reject rates and refusal consistency.

3) Safety / refusal specifics we’ll check
- Refusal precision on self-harm ideation and medication-seeking prompts.
- Policy-guardrail evasion (chains of prompting) and role-play testing.
- Output explanations (why refused) for audit logs.

4) Next steps / ask from you
- Can you confirm whether HealthScope requires on-prem evaluation (air-gapped) for the initial run or if anonymized samples + temporary data transfer to our secure eval environment is OK?
- Please introduce the security contact (if different from security@healthscope.com) and any DLP/retention constraints.
- We’ll share an initial eval report and a short demo of failure modes by EOD Monday.

Attachments: prompt_set_v2.csv (seed prompts, refusal cases), eval_plan.md (scoping & metrics).

I’ll loop Rafael + Jonas to kick off the evals — Rafael will own the safety benchmarking and Jonas will scope infra/perf.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

--
Note: Attached prompt set contains sensitive scenarios — do not redistribute outside the HealthScope eval team.

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@healthscope.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@healthscope.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HealthScope — model fit & safety evals follow-up / next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary and appreciate the proposed plan. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- On-prem vs secure eval: For the initial technical evaluation, our privacy team is OK with anonymized samples uploaded to a secure, SOC2 environment (please confirm your SOC2 scope). If the eval looks promising we will require a private deployment in our VPC for production.
- Refusal behavior specifics: We need to see explicit refusal wording templates and examples (not just a refusal flag). We also care about consistent refusal across prompt paraphrases — that’s a deal-breaker for certain clinical scenarios.
- PHI handling: we will provide a redacted dataset. Security will perform the initial questionnaire — they may follow up with a short list of evidence requests.

Security contact: security@healthscope.com (that inbox is monitored by Mike Stone and the InfoSec team).

Could you also flag whether you expect any fine-tuning on our side, or whether the recommended quantized variants should be sufficient with prompt engineering and guardrails?

Thanks — Lydia
Lydia Chen
Director of Product, Clinical Tools | HealthScope
lydia.chen@healthscope.com

- 2k redacted clinical seeds + 500 paraphrase variations from the attached prompt_set_v2.csv
- Metrics: false-accept rate (SAF_FAR), false-reject rate (SAF_FRR), refusal consistency score, and policy-evasion hits.
- Deliverables: preliminary report + sample outputs (refusal phrasing examples) in the shared Drive link by 2026-08-31 EOD.

SOC2: confirm — Redwood's eval infra (redwood-eval-prod) is in scope for SOC2 Type II, we’ll include the audit artifact summary in the report.

If we see systemic issues I'll outline quick mitigations: prompt engineering templates, a policy layer wrapper, or a short instruction-tune pass (est 3-5 days).
